content: Wikipedia is a collaborative platform that allows anyone to edit unprotected pages and save changes immediately. Once you make your first edit, you officially become a Wikipedia editor. To edit a page, click the edit this page tab at the top of the page or use the section-edit link. This action will open a new page containing a text box with the editable content of the original page. Below the edit box, you should provide a concise edit summary to describe your changes. You can use shorthand as described in the legend. Before saving, you can preview the differences between your edits and the previous version by clicking the Show changes button. If satisfied, click the Save page button to make your changes visible to all Wikipedia users. You can also access the Discussion tab to view the talk page, where other users leave comments about the page. To add a new section, click the + tab, or edit the page as you would an article. When leaving messages on talk pages or special-purpose project pages, remember to sign your comments. However, do not sign edits made to regular articles, as the MediaWiki software automatically tracks which user made each change in the page history. Minor Edits Marking an edit as minor indicates that the changes are superficial, such as correcting typos, adjusting formatting, or rearranging text without altering the content. Minor edits are considered non-controversial and do not require review. This option is available only to registered users. Major Edits For significant changes, it is recommended to discuss proposed edits on the article's talk page before proceeding. If working on a major edit over an extended period, using the {{inuse}} tag can help prevent edit conflicts. Once the edit is complete, include an edit summary to document the changes. These steps ensure that major edits are well-received by the Wikipedia community. Major edits should be reviewed to confirm consensus among editors, as any change affecting the meaning of an article is considered major, even if it involves only a single word. Wiki Markup Wikipedia uses a syntax system called wiki markup for formatting pages. For detailed guidance, refer to Help:Editing and Help:Wikitext examples. Links and URLs Only images uploaded to Wikipedia can be used. To upload an image, use the upload page, and find the uploaded image in the image list. Follow Wikipedia's image use policy for guidelines. For advanced image capabilities, refer to the topic on Extended image syntax. Headings To create a top-level heading, place it on a separate line surrounded by ==. For subheadings, use ===, ====, and so on. Character Formatting Certain formatting options allow the wiki to display text exactly as typed. This what you see is what you get approach ensures precise representation. Invisible Text (Comments) Hidden comments can be added within an article's text using a specific format. While uncommon, this practice is sometimes acceptable. Table of Contents (TOC) A page with at least four headers automatically generates a table of contents (TOC) before the first header. You can control the TOC's placement using __TOC__ or remove it entirely with __NOTOC__. Tables Tables can be created using special wiki markup or standard HTML elements. For guidance on when to use tables, refer to Wikipedia: When to use tables. Variables Variables like {{NUMBEROFARTICLES}} display the number of pages in the main namespace containing links and not redirects. Other variables, such as {{CURRENTMONTHNAMEGEN}}, provide grammatical forms of month names for specific languages. Templates Wikipedia supports templates, which are standardized text chunks that can be inserted into articles. For example, typing {{stub}} adds a message indicating that the article is a stub and inviting users to expand it. Common templates include {{disambig}} for disambiguation pages and {{sectstub}} for section stubs. For a complete list of templates, see Wikipedia: Template messages. By following these guidelines and best practices, you can contribute effectively to Wikipedia while maintaining the quality and integrity of its content.
